home-remodeling.title: Doral, FL Home Remodeling by PGX Builders Group
home-remodeling.meta_description: Whole-home remodeling in Doral, FL. PGX guts and rebuilds 1990s and 2000s homes — permitted through the City of Doral, supervised daily. Call (786) 273-2524.
home-remodeling.hero_sub: PGX Builders Group takes Doral homes built in the 1990s and 2000s down to their strengths and rebuilds them — permitted through the City of Doral, supervised daily, finished to the standard the address implies.
intro_paragraphs: Doral is young by Miami standards — most of its housing went up between the early 1990s and the 2010s, in gated communities like Doral Estates, Doral Isles, Costa del Sol, and the Islands at Doral. The construction is solid concrete block; the interiors are another story. Arched niches, beige tile in every room, a kitchen walled off from the family room — design decisions that made sense at the sales center in 2002. A whole-home remodel keeps the structure and replaces everything that dates the house: layout, mechanicals, lighting, flooring, openings.

Permitting is the City of Doral Building Department's business, and it reviews each discipline — structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical — as its own sub-permit and requires the contractor of record to be registered with the city. Before any of that, most Doral communities want their own say: nearly every neighborhood here is HOA-governed, and exterior changes typically pass through an architectural review committee first. Impact windows and doors must carry Miami-Dade product approvals, since all of Doral sits in the High Velocity Hurricane Zone. We sequence all three reviews so none of them stalls the others.

PGX runs whole-home projects the way they should be run: a fixed written scope priced before demolition, one licensed team (Lic. CGC1539072) from estimate through warranty, and a superintendent who walks the site every day it is active. In gated communities we handle guard-gate coordination, HOA paperwork, and the quiet logistics that keep neighbors friendly. After 20-plus years and more than 150 remodels and additions across South Florida, we have learned that the difference between a good remodel and a stressful one is rarely the tile. It is the management.

scope_items.desc: Miami-Dade approved impact glazing throughout, replacing builder windows and shutters, with HVHZ product approvals filed as part of the permit package.

scope_items.desc: Large-format porcelain or wood flooring, custom closets and built-ins, level-5 drywall, and lighting design that retires the vanilla can lights of the 2000s.

scope_items.desc: Architectural review submittals, guard-gate and vendor scheduling, city inspections, and final closeout, handled by us so the paperwork never becomes your hobby.

faqs.q: Do I need HOA approval before remodeling my home in Doral?
faqs.a: For interior-only work, usually not — your HOA cares about what it can see. The moment the scope touches windows, doors, the roof, or anything visible from the street, most Doral associations require architectural review committee approval alongside the city permit. We prepare those submittals as part of the project and sequence them so the HOA never becomes the bottleneck.

faqs.q: How long do City of Doral permits take for a whole-home remodel?
faqs.a: It depends on scope. Each discipline — structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical — is reviewed separately, and a full-gut package touches all of them. Clean, complete drawings can clear review in weeks; packages that draw comments go through revision cycles that add time. We cannot control the reviewer's queue, but we can control the quality of the submittal, which is where most delays are actually born.

faqs.q: Is it smarter to gut-renovate my 1990s Doral house or buy new construction?
faqs.a: If you like your community, your lot, and your commute, renovation usually wins. Doral's 1990s and 2000s houses have sound concrete-block structures; what ages is everything attached to them. A whole-home remodel gets you a current interior, new systems, and impact openings without surrendering an established neighborhood for a construction zone at the edge of the city. When the structure argues otherwise, we will tell you.

faqs.q: Can you replace all the windows with impact glass during the remodel?
faqs.a: Yes, and a whole-home remodel is the right moment to do it. All of Miami-Dade sits in the High Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every window and door must carry a current product approval and gets inspected after installation. Folding impact windows into the larger project means one permit package, one round of stucco and finish repairs, and shutters you never have to put up again.

faqs.q: How much does a full home remodel run in Doral?
faqs.a: Ranges are wide because scope is everything: finishes-and-fixtures refreshes sit at one end, full-gut projects with structural openings, new MEP systems, and impact windows at the other. We are a high-end contractor, so we will not be the cheapest number you collect — we will be the number that does not change after demolition. A walk-through gets you a fixed written scope and a real price.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Walk us through the house, tell us how you actually live, and we will put a real number on it — in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Doral, FL Kitchen Remodeling, Cabinetry & Stone | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Custom kitchen remodeling in Doral, FL — cabinetry, stone, islands, and layout changes for builder-era kitchens. Permitted and supervised. Call (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.h1: Doral kitchens, rebuilt from the studs
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters, and islands that actually fit the room — designed, permitted through the City of Doral, and installed under the daily supervision of a licensed South Florida general contractor.
intro_paragraphs: Doral kitchens mostly arrived with the production builders of the mid-1990s through the 2010s, and they share a family resemblance: raised breakfast bars, speckled granite, cabinets that stop a foot short of the ceiling, and a layout that keeps the cook walled off from everyone else. In Doral Estates, Vintage Estates, and the Isles at Grand Bay, owners are replacing all of it — taking the wall down, centering the room on a working island, and ordering cabinetry built for the space rather than pulled from a catalog.

A kitchen that only swaps doors and counters is simple. A kitchen that moves appliances, adds circuits, or opens a wall is a permitted project, and here that means the City of Doral Building Department — separate sub-permits for electrical, plumbing, and mechanical work, drawings for any structural opening, and a contractor registered with the city. Interior work rarely concerns your HOA, but a relocated vent hood or gas line concerns the inspectors, and it should. We produce the full permit package and schedule every inspection.

Kitchens are the remodel families live through, so we build them like guests in your house. Floors and adjacent rooms get protected, dust gets contained, and the crew shows up on the schedule taped to your fridge. Your written scope fixes the price before demolition, cabinetry and stone are ordered against confirmed field measurements, and one PGX supervisor answers for all of it. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072, with 20-plus years of South Florida kitchens behind us.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: From a cosmetic refresh to a full reconfiguration, every Doral kitchen we build starts with a written scope. Typical elements below.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry that reaches the ceiling
scope_items.desc: Built-to-order boxes and fronts, with interior fittings planned around how you actually cook rather than around a stock size chart.

scope_items.name: Islands sized for the family room
scope_items.desc: Quartz, quartzite, or natural marble templated after cabinets are set, scaled to Doral's open plans with seating on the correct side.

scope_items.name: Appliances for the opened-up plan
scope_items.desc: Relocating cooking and refrigeration to fit the new layout, including the gas, electrical, and venting rough-ins that each carry their own inspection.

scope_items.name: Taking down the kitchen wall
scope_items.desc: Engineered removal of the wall between kitchen and living space — the single change that does the most for a 2000s Doral floor plan.

scope_items.name: Light beyond one ceiling box
scope_items.desc: New circuits feeding task, ambient, and accent light where the builder left a single fixture and called it a day.

faqs.q: Is a permit required for kitchen remodeling in Doral?
faqs.a: For anything beyond cosmetics, yes. The City of Doral requires permits when a kitchen remodel touches electrical, plumbing, or mechanical work — which covers new circuits, moved sinks, relocated appliances, and vent hoods. Flooring alone does not need one in a single-family home. We pull every required sub-permit and schedule the inspections, so the project is as legal as it is pretty.

faqs.q: How many weeks should I plan for a kitchen remodel?
faqs.a: The honest answer has two clocks. Custom cabinetry carries a lead time measured in weeks to months, so we order it early against verified field measurements. On-site construction — demolition, rough-ins, inspections, installation, stone templating and setting — typically runs several weeks more. We sequence the two clocks so the kitchen is out of service for the build, not for the whole wait.

faqs.q: Can you remove the wall between my kitchen and family room?
faqs.a: In most Doral two-stories, that wall is doing structural work, which is why it needs an engineer, a beam, and a City of Doral permit rather than a Saturday and a sledgehammer. It is also the single most transformative change available to a builder-era floor plan. We handle the engineering, the permit drawings, and the temporary shoring, and the result looks inevitable rather than remodeled.

faqs.q: Why choose custom cabinetry over big-box kitchen packages?
faqs.a: Stock cabinets come in fixed sizes and make your room negotiate with them; custom cabinetry is built to your walls, your ceiling height, and your cooking habits. In practice that means no filler strips, storage in the awkward corners, and fronts that still look intentional in fifteen years. It costs more and takes longer, and in a home you plan to keep, it is the better spend.

faqs.q: Do gated communities in Doral make kitchen remodels harder?
faqs.a: They add logistics, not obstacles. Guard gates need contractor lists, some associations restrict work hours and delivery windows, and every community keeps its own vendor rules. We are used to it: our crews register properly, arrive when the community allows, and keep the site clean enough that your neighbors' curiosity stays friendly. Interior kitchen work itself rarely needs association approval.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring your ideas, photos, and grievances with the current layout. We will bring a measured plan and an honest number — in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodels in Doral, FL — Done Right | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Bathroom remodeling in Doral, FL. Garden tubs out, curbless showers and real waterproofing in — permitted through the City of Doral. Call (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.h1: Primary baths, minus the garden tub
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: PGX remodels Doral primary baths into stone, glass, and quiet luxury — fully permitted with the City of Doral and waterproofed to standards nobody sees but everybody benefits from.
intro_paragraphs: The primary bath in a 1990s or 2000s Doral home follows a formula: a corner garden tub nobody has filled since the housewarming, a small framed shower, cultured-marble counters, and a strip of Hollywood lights. Owners across Doral Isles, Costa del Sol, and Grand Bay Estates are trading that formula for the current one — a large curbless shower behind frameless glass, a freestanding tub if the room earns it, double vanities in real stone, and tile chosen by a human being.

Bathroom remodels in Doral pull permits through the City of Doral Building Department, with plumbing and electrical reviewed as separate sub-permits and inspections at the stages that matter — including the shower pan, which is tested before a single tile goes on. Relocating fixtures or adding a freestanding tub changes drain and supply runs, which is exactly the work you want inspected. Second-floor baths raise the stakes: a slow leak up there finishes the ceiling below in a way nobody ordered.

Waterproofing is where bathroom budgets are quietly won or lost, so PGX treats it as scope, not an afterthought: modern membrane systems, flood-tested pans, sealed niches and benches, all documented before tile hides the evidence. The rest of the job runs the PGX way — a fixed written price, materials confirmed before demolition, protected hallways in an occupied house, and a supervisor on site daily. One licensed team, Lic. CGC1539072, from the first measurement to the warranty call you probably will not need.

scope_items.desc: Frameless glass, linear drains, and slope built into the floor — the old corner tub almost always gives the new shower room to breathe.

scope_items.desc: Membrane systems and flood-tested pans installed to manufacturer spec and inspected by the city before tile goes down. Unseen, and non-negotiable.

scope_items.desc: Placed with the floor-mounted filler, reinforcement, and drain relocation planned in drawings first, so the showpiece never becomes a plumbing improvisation.

scope_items.name: Vanities and quiet ventilation
scope_items.desc: Custom double vanities, ventilation sized to the room, and layered lighting that flatters at 7 a.m. better than a Hollywood strip ever did.

faqs.q: Does remodeling a bathroom in Doral involve permits?
faqs.a: If the project moves or adds plumbing fixtures, changes electrical, or alters walls, the City of Doral requires permits with separate plumbing and electrical sub-permits, plus inspections at rough-in and at the shower pan. A purely cosmetic swap — new mirror, new paint, new hardware — does not. Most remodels worth doing land on the permitted side of that line, and we manage all of it.

faqs.q: Can a garden tub be replaced with a walk-in shower?
faqs.a: Yes — it is the most requested bathroom change in Doral's 1990s and 2000s housing, and the tub's footprint usually gives the new shower generous dimensions. The work involves drain relocation, framing, membrane waterproofing, and a flood test before tile, all permitted and inspected. Done properly, you gain a shower you use daily in place of a tub that mostly collected dust.

faqs.q: How do you keep a second-floor bathroom from leaking?
faqs.a: With redundancy that gets verified, not assumed: membrane waterproofing over the whole wet area, a flood-tested pan witnessed before tile is set, sealed penetrations, and inspected plumbing connections. Second-floor baths are where shortcuts eventually introduce themselves through the ceiling below, so we document the waterproofing stage with photos before it disappears behind stone. It is unglamorous work, and it is the entire point.

faqs.q: How long is a primary bathroom out of service during a remodel?
faqs.a: Plan on several weeks from demolition to final inspection, driven by rough-in work, inspections, waterproofing cure times, and tile setting done at the pace good tile setting requires. We confirm materials are in hand before demolition starts so the bathroom is never torn open and waiting on a backorder. If the house has a second bath, life continues almost normally.

faqs.q: How do your crews work inside a gated Doral community?
faqs.a: By the community's rules, which we ask for before day one: registered vendor lists at the guard gate, work hours the association actually enforces, and parking where it belongs. Inside the house we contain dust at the bathroom door, protect the floors along the route, and haul debris out daily. Discretion is part of the service, not an upgrade.

home-additions.meta_description: Home additions in Doral, FL — rear extensions, second stories, and in-law suites with HOA and City of Doral approvals handled. Call PGX at (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.hero_sub: Home additions for Doral — rear extensions, second stories, and in-law suites, engineered and permitted through the City of Doral, built by one licensed team that keeps the rest of the house livable.
home-additions.local_heading: Room to grow in a built-out city
intro_paragraphs: Doral families tend to stay put — the schools, the communities, and the commute all argue for it — but the houses built here in the 1990s and 2000s were sized for a different chapter. So owners in the Islands at Doral, Doral Park, and Doral Isles add instead of moving: a rear extension that gives the kitchen and family room real square footage, a bedroom wing for in-laws who visit for months, or a second-story addition where the lot has nothing left to give.

Additions get the full treatment from the City of Doral Building Department: zoning review for setbacks and lot coverage, structural drawings for foundations and tie-beams, and every trade permitted and inspected. In Doral's gated communities the HOA architectural committee reviews the addition as well, usually before ground breaks, and each association holds opinions about rooflines, finishes, and construction hours. The new roof structure must meet High Velocity Hurricane Zone requirements like everything else in Miami-Dade. None of this should shrink your plans — it just rewards a contractor who files clean drawings the first time.

The test of an addition is whether anyone can find the seam. PGX matches existing stucco texture, ties new roof framing into old cleanly, and levels new slabs to existing floors so the house reads as one thought. We phase the work to keep your family in the home, seal the construction zone off from daily life, and put a supervisor on site every working day. The scope is fixed in writing before we pour anything, and one team — licensed, insured, Lic. CGC1539072 — carries the project from engineering through final inspection.

faqs.q: Will my Doral HOA approve a home addition?
faqs.a: Most associations approve additions that respect the community's architectural language — matching rooflines, tile, stucco profiles, and approved colors. The review runs through your HOA's architectural committee, usually before the City of Doral issues permits, and the quality of your drawings sets the tone. We prepare submittal packages that answer the committee's questions before they are asked, which is the fastest route through.

faqs.q: How much can I build on my lot in Doral?
faqs.a: Zoning decides: lot coverage, setbacks, and height limits vary by district and are reviewed by the City of Doral during permitting, and your HOA's rules can be tighter than the city's. Many Doral lots in gated communities are efficient rather than sprawling, which is why second-story additions earn a look when the footprint has no room left. We evaluate both sets of rules before you fall in love with a floor plan.

faqs.q: Can my one-story house support a second-story addition?
faqs.a: Sometimes as-built, often with reinforcement, occasionally not economically — the answer lives in your foundation and walls, and a structural engineer finds it before anyone commits. Doral's concrete-block construction is a good starting point, but footings and tie-beams were sized for the house that exists, not the one you want. We coordinate the structural evaluation up front so the decision is informed, not hopeful.

faqs.q: Will the new addition need impact windows and doors?
faqs.a: Yes. New construction in Doral must meet the Florida Building Code's High Velocity Hurricane Zone provisions, which means impact-rated windows and doors with current Miami-Dade product approvals, engineered roof connections, and inspections to match. This is a feature, not a burden — the newest part of your house will also be its strongest, and it never needs shutters.

faqs.q: What does a home addition cost in Doral?
faqs.a: Additions run costlier per square foot than interior remodeling because you are buying structure — foundations, roof, walls, and the careful surgery of tying new construction into old. Scope, finishes, and structural complexity move the number more than size does. We give you a fixed written price after design, and we hold it, which matters more over a six-month project than the first estimate ever does.

home-additions.cta_sub: Tell us what the house is missing. We will look at the lot, the zoning, and the structure, then give you a straight answer — in English o en español.

outdoor-living.hero_sub: Summer kitchens, covered terraces, and pergolas — outdoor living built for Doral's lake and golf-course lots, HOA-approved, permitted through the City of Doral, and engineered for hurricane country.
outdoor-living.local_heading: The lot is half the house
intro_paragraphs: Doral backyards come with assets other Miami suburbs envy — lake frontage across Doral Isles and the Islands at Doral, golf views in Doral Estates and Costa del Sol — and most of them are still wearing the builder's original screened patio and a strip of pavers. Owners are upgrading to genuine outdoor rooms: covered terraces with tongue-and-groove ceilings, summer kitchens with real ventilation, pergolas with actual engineering, and travertine or porcelain decks that treat the yard as living space instead of a view.

Outdoor work is where Doral's HOA architectural committees pay closest attention, because all of it is visible: pergolas, pavers, exterior paint colors, even the driveway. Approvals go through your association and the City of Doral Building Department, and structures like pergolas and roofed terraces must be engineered for High Velocity Hurricane Zone wind loads — a pergola that is not anchored for a storm is just future debris. Summer kitchens add gas and electrical sub-permits. We prepare drawings that satisfy both reviewers in one pass, which is quicker than learning their preferences by rejection.

Exterior projects reward a single accountable contractor, because the trades stack: the terrace slab before the summer kitchen, the stucco before the paint, the roof tie-ins before any ceiling closes. PGX sequences all of it under one fixed written scope and one daily supervisor, coordinating re-roofs and impact openings alongside the outdoor build so the house gets disturbed once instead of four times. We have spent 20-plus years building outdoors in South Florida, which is long enough to respect the sun, the rain, and the HOA.

scope_items.desc: Grills, ventilation, refrigeration, and stone counters with the gas and electrical runs permitted through the city — an outdoor room that actually cooks.

faqs.q: Do I need approval for a pergola or summer kitchen in Doral?
faqs.a: Two approvals, usually: your HOA's architectural committee, because outdoor structures are visible, and the City of Doral Building Department, because pergolas, roofed terraces, and outdoor kitchens are permitted construction. Gas, electrical, and plumbing to a summer kitchen each carry their own sub-permit. We submit to both reviewers in parallel with drawings each one recognizes, which keeps a backyard project from becoming a correspondence project.

faqs.q: Can a pergola actually survive hurricane season?
faqs.a: An engineered one can. In the High Velocity Hurricane Zone, shade structures need calculated wind loads, proper footings, and anchoring designed for uplift — the failure mode is not the pergola falling down but taking off. We build pergolas and covered terraces to engineered drawings with inspected connections, which is the difference between outdoor architecture and future storm debris.

faqs.q: What decking holds up best on a Doral lake lot?
faqs.a: Travertine stays cooler underfoot and looks at home with Doral's Mediterranean housing; porcelain pavers offer sharper, more contemporary lines and shrug off stains. Both handle sun and rain well when the base and drainage under them are done right, which is where lakefront lots deserve extra attention — water should leave your terrace on your terms. We install both and will show you each in place.

faqs.q: Can you coordinate a re-roof with the outdoor project?
faqs.a: Yes, and you should want it coordinated. Tie-ins between a new covered terrace and the existing roof involve flashing details and warranty boundaries that go wrong when two uncoordinated contractors meet on one roofline. PGX sequences roofing alongside the terrace structure so waterproofing details are owned by one accountable team, and the house gets opened up once rather than twice.

faqs.q: How disruptive is backyard construction to daily life?
faqs.a: Less than interior work, with honest caveats: there will be concrete trucks, saw cutting, and a stretch when the yard belongs to us. We route crews away from the interior entirely, protect driveways and landscaping, follow your community's work-hour rules, and leave the site tidy each evening. Most families barely change their routine until it is time to argue over who gets the outdoor kitchen first.

Two decades of owners have since screened terraces, turned patios into offices, converted garages, swapped water heaters and air handlers, and had impact windows installed by whoever answered the phone. Some of that was permitted. The rest sits quietly in the house until a title company, a lender or an insurance underwriter goes looking for the paperwork.

Permits are filed with the City of Doral Building Department, which reviews structural, electrical, plumbing and mechanical work as separate sub-permits and requires the contractor of record to be registered with the city before anything is issued. Doral only incorporated in 2003, so a large share of the housing here was permitted by Miami-Dade County, and those older records still live in the county's system. Every exterior opening and roof system needs HVHZ product approval. Condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories or more carry milestone inspections and a reserve study on top of all that.

We treat permitting as construction management rather than errands. PGX pulls the record on your address, retains the engineer or architect the drawings genuinely require, and assembles a package that gives plan review nothing to ask twice. Comments get answered in writing. Inspections are scheduled and attended by our own superintendent instead of left to a subcontractor's morning. What you end up with is a fixed written scope, one licensed team (Lic. CGC1539072) accountable from first filing to final closeout, and a file that reads clean when a buyer's attorney opens it.

faqs.q: A title search on my Doral house turned up an open permit. What now?
faqs.a: First we find out what it actually is. Some open records are jobs that were never finished. Some expired mid-project. Plenty are jobs completed years ago where nobody ever called the final inspection. That last kind usually ends with an inspection and a closeout. The first kind can mean opening up finished work or permitting it again. You get that answer in writing, well before your closing date.

faqs.q: The permit is from Miami-Dade County, not the City of Doral. Who closes it?
faqs.a: Doral only became a city in 2003, so anything permitted before that was approved by the county, which covers a good part of Doral Estates, Doral Park and the older sections. Those records still sit in the county's system while the property now answers to the city. The first step is establishing which office closes the file and what it wants to see, and that depends on the type of work. We do that research before you spend money on drawings.

faqs.q: My HOA already approved the work. Do I still need a city permit?
faqs.a: Yes. Architectural review approval and a building permit are two different animals, and nearly every community here has the first: Doral Isles, the Islands at Doral, Vintage Estates, Grand Bay Estates. The association is deciding whether the work fits the neighborhood. The city is deciding whether it meets code. An HOA letter will not satisfy an inspector, a lender or a title company, and it will not close a permit.

faqs.q: Do my impact windows need Miami-Dade product approval?
faqs.a: In practice, yes. Doral sits inside the High Velocity Hurricane Zone, so every window, door and roof system needs approval documentation valid for the HVHZ, and Miami-Dade's Notice of Acceptance is the version inspectors here see most. Approval alone is not enough: the installation has to match the anchor type, spacing and substrate the document specifies. Openings put in without that paperwork fail inspection, and can quietly cost you wind mitigation credit on your insurance.

faqs.q: Does the 40-year recertification apply to my house or my building in Doral?
faqs.a: Not to a single-family home or a duplex. Miami-Dade's building recertification program exempts both. It does reach Doral's condominium, rental and commercial buildings, and the county has since tightened that old forty-year cycle, so buildings of the vintage that fills this city come up for a first recertification well before forty. Condominium and cooperative buildings three habitable stories and up also carry state milestone inspections and a structural integrity reserve study. The repair work those reports generate is work we do.
